title: AI Chatbots Will Help Students Learn Nothing Faster Than Ever
author: Dan Meyer
summary: Meyer responds to Sal Khan's TED talk on Khanmigo by arguing that the chatbot demos, though genuinely novel, all operate on extremely small units of learning. He contrasts small questions such as how to solve one expression with large ones such as who am I and do I belong here, which chatbots do not address. His central claim is that chatbot boosters hold a wrong model of schooling as the sum of small units that can be unbundled from relationships, context and time. He backs this with a history of earlier unbundling promises from explanation videos, auto-graded exercises and Udacity. He speculates that technologists' own schooling made them see the large units as dispensable. The conclusion is that AI will speed up learning of tiny ideas while the human relationships in schooling remain where its value lies.
points: Khanmigo's demos are novel but confined to small learning units, so they define the limits of what chatbots can do in schools.
Schooling cannot be unbundled into small units because students cannot separate how to factor an expression from who they are and whether they belong.
The unbundling model has a track record of failure, from Khan's 2011 videos and 2016 exercises to Udacity at San Jose State, without proponents being asked to account for it.
Technologists may favour the model because they personally needed little from the large units of schooling, unlike most families who want warmer relationships at school.
Work that amplifies the relationships within schooling is safe from chatbots, while businesses built on tiny learning units are exposed.
quotes: I want to offer that these demos are mostly very novel and unlike anything I have ever seen from digital technology. Here I am on the same side of most chatbot boosters—including venture capitalists, tech journalists, Sal Khan, and many others.

But schooling is no more the sum of small learning units than the human body is the sum of its bones. Nor is it any easier to unbundle relationships, context, time, or other humans from schooling than it is to unbundle someone’s heart from their body.

Their model for schooling hasn’t worked. It didn’t work when Sal Khan suggested explanation videos would transform education in 2011. It didn’t work when he suggested auto-graded exercises would transform education in 2016.
In their own schooling, they learned very quickly by themselves. They often perceived themselves (perhaps rightly) as more intelligent than their peers or even their teachers.

They are not clamoring for a digital substitute for human relationship. They have not wanted that historically and are not going to start now, even though the chatbots are smarter and quicker with smaller units of learning than ever before.

AI chatbots are most effective as the unit size of learning asymptotically approaches nothing. They will help students learn nothing faster than ever. Anyone in the extremely small units of learning business is in a lot of trouble.
